sections.subtitle: Projected total population, 2022 to 2047
sections.footer: Source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Population change on the Isles of Scilly in 2032

The population on the Isles of Scilly is projected to decrease from 2,281 people in 2022 to 2,177 people in 2032.

There are seven areas in England where the population is projected to decrease in this period.

The biggest factor in this population change is births and deaths, which will decrease the population by 110 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change on the Isles of Scilly
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. On the Isles of Scilly, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 110, with 190 births and 300 deaths on the Isles of Scilly between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population on the Isles of Scilly by 4.8%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 32, with 3,086 people moving to the area and 3,054 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population on the Isles of Scilly by 1.4%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 34, with 247 people moving to the area and 213 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population on the Isles of Scilly by 1.5%.
  • Net international migration is projected to reduce the population by 54, with 28 people moving to the area and 82 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population on the Isles of Scilly by 2.4%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile on the Isles of Scilly in 2032

The median age on the Isles of Scilly is projected to remain the same at 45 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 23% of the population on the Isles of Scilly are projected to be aged 65 years or over, down from 25% in 2022.

sections.title: The 70 to 79 age group are set to see the largest change on the Isles of Scilly between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) on the Isles of Scilly is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to fall from 417 to 343 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change on the Isles of Scilly?

In 2032, 17% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, around the same as in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups on the Isles of Scilly between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will rise from 6% to 7%
